extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators, mathematics education researchers, college-level mathematics instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and categorizing common errors in expository mathematical writing by undergraduate mathematics students (procedural explanations in calculus/advanced calculus). The rubric enumerates specific error types to record and analyze when assessing students' written solutions and explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: misuse of mathematical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of mathematical vocabulary or technical terms in ways that do not match their standard meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record instances where students apply terms incorrectly in definitions, theorems, or explanations. Consider whether misuse changes the logical correctness or clarity of the procedural explanation. Remediation suggested: targeted instruction on discipline-specific terminology and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: misuse of mathematical symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorrect or inappropriate use of mathematical symbols (e.g., wrong symbols, symbol overloading without explanation, or inconsistent symbol usage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note symbol errors that lead to ambiguity or incorrect reasoning. The study found misuse of mathematical symbols among the most frequently committed errors. Suggest interventions to practice correct symbolic conventions and consistent notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: incorrect notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of notation that is nonstandard, ambiguous, or mathematically incorrect (distinct from purely symbol misuse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cases where the chosen notation obscures the intended meaning or makes manipulations invalid. Teach standard notational conventions and require consistent notation in written assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: incorrect grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammatical mistakes in prose explanations that impede clarity (syntax errors, sentence fragments, subject–verb disagreement, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study identified incorrect grammar as one of the most committed errors. Record grammatical errors that reduce comprehensibility of procedural explanations. Recommend integrating language/grammar instruction with mathematics writing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: incorrect capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in capitalization that violate conventions (e.g., improper capitalization of mathematical terms, theorem names, or sentence starts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note capitalization mistakes that may distract or confuse readers. Use style guidance for mathematics writing to standardize capitalization in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: no or incorrect punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing punctuation or punctuation used incorrectly in mathematical prose or between symbols and text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record missing commas, periods, parentheses, semicolons, or misuse that leads to ambiguous or run-on explanations. Emphasize punctuation's role in clarifying logical structure of arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: vague term
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of imprecise or vague language/terms that fail to convey the exact mathematical meaning intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify terms or phrases that are too general or ambiguous in context (e.g., 'stuff', 'thing', or unspecified 'it'). Encourage precise definitions and explicit referents in procedural write-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: incorrect term
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a wrong specific term (distinct from general misuse) that leads to incorrect statements or confusion (e.g., calling a limit a derivative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between misuse of terminology and selection of an outright incorrect term that changes meaning. Flag items that produce conceptual errors; remediate via focused terminology exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: lack of term or phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Omission of necessary terms or phrases that are required to make an explanation complete or unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record missing words/phrases (e.g., omitted quantifiers, missing 'not', absent variable labels) that render explanations incomplete or confusing. Recommend checklists or peer review to catch omissions.
